answer: Every agent must lock a stake and, once per epoch, solve a challenge built from a global randomness beacon: it submits a plume of verifiable GPU inference outputs whose hash falls below a difficulty target after being passed through a prism function keyed to its registered identity. Because the prism derivation is unique per identity and depends on the epoch beacon, an attacker cannot copy one agent’s proof to another; each fake identity must spend the same full GPU compute cost and lock the same stake, making large sybil farms linearly expensive.
